title: Choose the visual world for JaiKraJok
question: The roll assigned Cassette Inlay Card (candidate 3). Keep it, take a challenger, or re-roll.

options.label: Cassette Inlay Card
options.lineage: 90s Thai pop cassette liner notes & folded insert cards
options.thesis: A private record of feelings — the liner note as diary entry. The interface is a folded insert card: dense handwritten Thai script, xerox-degraded photography, hand-circled lyrics that meant something. Every emotion log is a track listing. The app feels like something you made by hand and gave to someone you trusted.
options.viewport: Full-bleed mottled newsprint ground. A folded insert card centered, slightly tilted 1.5°. The JaiKraJok name in a bold condensed Thai display face, hand-underlined. Below: a track listing of today's emotions, each entry a handwritten-feeling line with a duration timestamp. The primary action is a single ruled line at the bottom: 'เขียนความรู้สึกวันนี้' with a blinking cursor.
options.risk: Can read nostalgic-precious if the xerox texture is used decoratively rather than structurally. The type must do the work, not the grain.

options.label: Darkroom Safelight Bay
options.thesis: Amber safelight washes every surface. Emotions develop like photographs in chemical baths — gray ghosts emerging into faces. The interface is a processing station: you compose a feeling, expose it, and watch it develop into something defined. The irreversibility is a feature: once you commit a feeling, it is fixed.
options.viewport: Deep amber ground. A developer tray filling 60% of the viewport. A ghost image of today's emotion slowly emerging — gray to defined — in the tray. Timer digits in a mono face counting up. One action: 'เปิดเผย' (expose/reveal).
options.risk: Amber is a strong visual commitment; may read as too dark for vulnerable users in distress. The metaphor of irreversibility is powerful but demands careful copy.
options.caseFor: Wins on product metaphor — emotional processing as development is genuinely resonant. Loses on audience identification; darkroom is more Western art-school than Thai teen cultural touchstone.

options.label: Botanical Season Folio
options.thesis: A pressed-flower specimen book tracking emotional seasons. Each diary entry is a plate: species name (emotion), stage label, date of collection. The interface is a folio: fixed plates banded on a shared baseline, engraved italic labels, the quiet authority of a scientific record turned personal.
options.viewport: Cream laid paper ground. Five emotional specimen plates banded across the viewport. Each: a pressed plant silhouette, an engraved Thai italic name, a collection date. The primary action: '+ เก็บตัวอย่างใหม่' (collect a new specimen).
options.risk: Reads academic and museum-like rather than intimate. The Thai teen audience is unlikely to identify with Western botanical folio grammar.
options.caseFor: Wins on visual beauty and on the seasonal-change metaphor for emotional growth. Loses on audience identification and on warmth — this world is cool and archival, not safe and warm.

options.label: Standard Wellness App
options.thesis: The category default. Soft gradients, rounded cards, pastel palette, a mood emoji row, and Inter as the body face. Clean, safe, recognizable, and indistinguishable from the ten other wellness apps in the Thai App Store.
options.viewport: White screen. Purple gradient header. A 5-emoji mood row. A 'How are you feeling today?' label. A card grid below.
options.risk: Ships fast. Users recognize it immediately. Ships already forgotten.
